conversion_plan.kp_title: Identifying Correct Statements About a Matrix
conversion_plan.problem_before:
Consider the matrix 
$C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}].$
Which of the following statements are true?

- $C$ is upper triangular
- $C$ is lower triangular
- ${C}^{T}$ is upper triangular

$A=\begin{bmatrix}8 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix},\,B=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 5 & 7 & 11\end{bmatrix},\,C=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0\end{bmatrix}.$

Consider the matrix 
$A=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}.$
Which of the following statements are true?

I. $A$ is upper triangular

II. $A$ is lower triangular

III. ${A}^{T}$ is lower triangular

all_false_original.proof: A has nonzero entries below its main diagonal (a32=1), and above (a13=-3). Thus A is neither upper nor lower triangular. Transposition moves a32=1 above the diagonal, so A^T is not lower triangular either. All three statements are false.
